title: 1954 AHSME Problem 26
statement: The straight line \(AB\) is divided at \(C\) so that \(\overline{AC}=3\overline{CB}.\) Circles are described on \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{CB}\) as diameters and a common tangent meets \(\overline{AB}\) produced at \(D.\) Then \(\overline{BD}\) equals:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: the diameter of the smaller circle

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the radius of the smaller circle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: the radius of the larger circle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the difference of the two radii

solutions.text:
Let \(\overline{CB}=u,\) so \(\overline{AC}=3u\) and \(\overline{AB}=4u.\) Measured from \(A,\) the circle centers are at \(\frac{3u}{2}\) and \(\frac{7u}{2},\) and their radii are in the ratio \(3:1.\) If \(AD=z,\) the common external tangent makes \(D\) the external center of similitude, so \[ \frac{z-\frac32u}{z-\frac72u}=3. \] Hence \(z=\frac{9u}{2},\) and \[ BD=z-4u=\frac u2, \] which is the radius of the smaller circle.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The point \(D\) is the external center of similitude of the two circles
Let \(\overline{CB}=u\) and compare the distances from \(D\) to the two centers in the ratio \(3:1\)
